You arrive in Baldur’s Gate shortly after leaving the Stronghold—having just helped beat back the Absolute—and find the city tense over an influx of refugees. Off‑screen, small anti‑refugee demonstrations have sprung up; Saer Grotpoll is the local agitator rallying “true Baldurians” while a Flaming Fist constable (Fist Lochan) tries to keep the crowd under control. Halsin is present and opposes the protest, so the player’s lines function as on‑the‑spot choices to either claim local status or defend the refugees; Saer’s tone shifts accordingly (from apologetic to scornful or dismissive). This is a brief civic encounter to convey local hostility and test the player’s stance—its specifics don’t alter the larger campaign beats already in motion (Netherstone, allies to recruit, tadpole/Prism concerns).
